candidates.title: Epoch listener never fetches the backlog inputs that the referee leaves pending past the input limit per epoch, so the honest operator aborts on the next epoch forever
candidates.component: PRT epoch listener and player process (doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua, doc/recipes/crisium.lua) against DaveConsensus v3.0.0-alpha.7
candidates.role: Support (implementation of an honest operator that no deployment runs; stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua open_epochs (lines 238-268: input_begin = previous_seal.inputIndexUpperBound, first_input_block = previous_seal.log.blockNumber); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua methods:poll (line 37 get_logs(address, self.first_input_block, ...), lines 72-73 'input stream has a gap or duplicate', lines 95-99 'sealed input count mismatch'), M.new (lines 165-167). Referee side: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol _nextInputIndexUpperBound and acceptStagedTournamentResult.
candidates.description: DaveConsensus seals an epoch with at most MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 2^24 pending inputs ('excess inputs stay pending', _nextInputIndexUpperBound = lowerBound + min(pending, 2^24)). The inputs past the limit were logged by the InputBox BEFORE the block of that seal and belong to the next epoch. crisium opens the listener of epoch N+1 with input_begin = seal N's inputIndexUpperBound, which is right, but with first_input_block = the block number of seal N, and prt-epoch.lua fetches InputAdded logs only from first_input_block on (its own comment: 'only from the block that sealed the previous epoch on'). The listener of epoch N skipped those inputs on purpose ('an input ... past the epoch's input limit, belongs to a later player'), and the listener of epoch N+1 never sees them. The first input it does see has an index above input_begin, so 'assert(index == self.input_begin + #self.inputs, "input stream has a gap or duplicate")' fails; if no later input arrives, the seal of N+1 fails 'sealed input count mismatch'. Both are uncaught errors in pass(), so the process exits, prt-supervise.sh relaunches it, and the relaunch derives the same first_input_block and fails again. The honest validator (and the sentinel, which uses the same listener) can never deliver epoch N+1's inputs, never seals its player, never computes or joins with the honest claim for epoch N+1, and never opens any later epoch. The same root cause applies to any epoch whose inputs precede the block the listener starts from, for example a DaveConsensus deployed for an application that already has inputs (constructor seals epoch 0 with [0, min(n, 2^24)) while the listener of epoch 0 starts at the consensus deployment block).
candidates.trigger: Any party that sends more than 2^24 inputs to the application's InputBox entry between two consecutive seals (while one epoch is disputed and settled). Section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'. No bond, no claim, no special ordering is needed. Cost is about 2^24 addInput calls; the dispute of the current epoch can be stretched by claims to give more time.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from the pinned referee: DaveConsensus.acceptStagedTournamentResult caps the sealed range and leaves the rest pending, and InputBox.addInput has no rate limit. The state (inputIndexUpperBound of a seal below getNumberOfInputs at that block) is exactly the case the listener's own MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH branch was written for. Experiment with the limit lowered to 4 (the module reads cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH when loaded; logic unchanged) reproduces both aborts with the real prt-epoch.lua.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The trigger is on-chain inputs, an adversary capability of section 7 ('Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'); no reorganization, API misuse or A1-A8 violation is needed (A3 is met: 'The input record assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch'). 2 Role: AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.' Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3 High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium' applies, because in the honest-operator role step 4 gives Critical. 4 Critical in the stood-for role: R4 'The honest operator defends every epoch whose dispute is open ... It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3)' and section 1 completeness failure 'The honest operator ... cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.' 5 Low: not reached.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure of the reference honest operator: from the first epoch with a backlog on, no honest claim is posted, so any claim a dishonest party posts for that epoch wins the root tournament by default and the application settles a state the state transition function does not define. The sentinel dies the same way, so no anomaly is reported either.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERCHAIN/backlog.lua (real prt-epoch.lua, fake chain as in the recipe's own listener fixture, limit lowered to 2^2). Epoch 2 delivers 4 of 6 inputs and seals [0,4). The listener of epoch 3, created as crisium does (input_begin 4, first_input_block = block of seal 2), delivers 0 of the 2 backlog inputs. Then: seal of epoch 3 with [4,6) -> 'prt-epoch.lua:96: sealed input count mismatch'; or a new input 6 -> 'prt-epoch.lua:73: input stream has a gap or duplicate'.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with a fake chain (or the harness chain with a consensus whose limit is patched down): lower cartesi.ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH before requiring prt-epoch, log MAX+2 inputs, seal epoch N with MAX of them, then open the listener of epoch N+1 with the arguments crisium computes (input_begin = seal upper bound, first_input_block = seal block) and seal epoch N+1 with [MAX, MAX+2). Required: the listener delivers inputs MAX and MAX+1 to its player and accepts the seal (exit 0). On audit/prt2 it raises (exit 1).

candidates.title: Dispute bridge fetches, keeps and re-sorts every log of the shared tournament factory since the epoch's seal, so its per-tick cost and memory grow with tournaments that anyone creates
candidates.component: PRT dispute bridge and log history (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua, doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua) against MultiLevelTournamentFactory of Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:observe lines 57-59 (addresses = { self.factory, self.consensus, self.root }, all from self.first_block, no topics), 68-87 (every fetched log appended to logs and decoded), 110-127 (table.sort over all logs, every event appended to events), methods:jobs line 373 (loop over all events), report_lost_matches; doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua get_logs_of/fetch (logs kept per address for the life of the history). Referee side: prt/contracts/src/tournament/factories/MultiLevelTournamentFactory.sol instantiate() is external, unrestricted and emits TournamentCreated.
candidates.description: The bridge needs one factory log per epoch: the TournamentCreated of its root, which is in the seal's block. It nevertheless asks eth_getLogs for every log of the factory address from the seal block to the observation head on every observation, without a topic or address-argument filter, stores them all in history.logs[factory] until the epoch's bridge is retired, and on every observe() copies all of them into a fresh array, sorts that array, walks it decoding every event, and returns every event in snapshot.events, which jobs() and the sentinel walk again. The factory is shared by every Dave application that uses it, and MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate(initialHash, provider) can be called by anyone for any hash and provider; each call emits one TournamentCreated from the factory. So the cost of one tick of the honest bridge, the memory of the process, and the cost of a restart (which refetches from the seal block) all grow linearly (n log n for the sort) with chain activity that has nothing to do with the application. tick() calls observe() at least twice per attempted job (refresh at the start and again in attempt()). prt-epoch.lua shows the intended treatment for the other shared contract ('The InputBox is shared by every application, so only this application's inputs are fetched'); the factory got no such filter.
candidates.trigger: A chain-level adversary (or simply other applications) calling factory.instantiate() repeatedly while an epoch of the victim application is in dispute. No bond and no relation to the application are needed; each call costs the gas of one clone creation.
candidates.reachability: Always reachable on a deployment whose factory is shared or public, which is every deployment of the pinned factory (instantiate has no access control). Measured with the real prt-bridge.lua and prt-log-history.lua on a fake chain, with pre-decoded events (so real decoding and JSON would add to it): an observation with nothing new costs 0.007 s with 1,000 foreign TournamentCreated logs, 1.06 s with 100,000 and 13.2 s with 1,000,000 (longer than an Ethereum block), and all of them are retained (history.logs.factory, snapshot.logs and snapshot.events each hold N+1 or N+2 entries).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. Section 7 lists the capability: 'Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application, such as inputs to other applications that share its input record.' 2 Role: support (AUDIT.md: the PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes are Support); section 3: Medium 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. 3 High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'; in the honest-operator role it is not one of the High cases (the cost is unbounded, not a constant factor within the sizing). 4 Critical in the stood-for role: R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records, and restarting, has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match, and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open. That total must not grow with the application's age, with the number of past epochs, or with chain activity that does not belong to the application.' 5 Low: not reached.
candidates.threat_to_goal: R4 requires that 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' Every move of the honest claim waits for at least two observations; once an observation takes longer than a block, the main loop of crisium never reaches its idle step (it only idles when the tip did not change), so the open epoch's pending inputs are not executed either, and with enough foreign logs the process exhausts memory or misses a responder deadline, which eliminates the honest claim (section 1, completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERCHAIN/factory.lua N (bridge.new_observer on a fake chain with one root creation, one seal and N foreign TournamentCreated logs on the factory after the seal block). Output: foreign=0 kept_factory_logs=1 observe_again=0.000s; foreign=1000 kept=1001 0.007s; foreign=100000 kept=100001 1.056s; foreign=1000000 kept=1000001 13.154s.
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic Lua test on a fake chain (or on the harness chain by calling factory.instantiate k times): observe once, add k TournamentCreated logs of unrelated tournaments on the factory after the seal block, observe again, and assert that the number of logs the bridge retains and returns (#history.logs[factory], #snapshot.logs, #snapshot.events) does not grow with k (exit 0 when independent of k, exit 1 on audit/prt2 where each equals k plus a constant). On the real chain the same assertion can be made on the eth_getLogs filter: the request for the factory must select the root's creation only.

candidates.title: Epoch listener re-sorts and re-checks every log of the open epoch on every poll, so one empty block costs time proportional to all inputs received so far (32 s at 100,000 inputs)
candidates.component: PRT epoch listener (doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua) as driven by doc/recipes/crisium.lua pass()
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua less (lines 20-23: four evmu.bint conversions per comparison), methods:poll lines 35-47 (all logs of both addresses copied and table.sort(logs, less) on every poll), lines 52-66 (a key string built and checked for every log on every poll); doc/recipes/crisium.lua pass() lines 299-303 (every listener polls before any dispute bridge ticks) and the main loop lines 361-381 (idle work only runs when the tip did not change).
candidates.description: Until its epoch is sealed, the listener's poll() rebuilds the full list of the epoch's InputAdded and consensus logs from its history, sorts the whole list with a comparator that parses four hex quantities into big integers per comparison, and then walks the whole list building and comparing an identity string per log, even when the observation brought no new log. The cost of observing one block is therefore O(n log n) in the number n of inputs already received in the open epoch, with a large constant, instead of a bounded cost per new input. crisium runs every listener's poll before it ticks any dispute bridge, so this time is added to every move of the epoch under dispute, and since the loop only does idle work (running the open epoch's pending inputs) when the tip has not changed, a poll longer than a block interval also stops the stored player from executing inputs until the seal, where epoch_sealed runs them all at once inside the pass.
candidates.trigger: An input sender who adds many cheap inputs to the application during one epoch (section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts, with payloads chosen to maximize the honest operator's cost (R12)'). 100,000 inputs, 0.6% of the 2^24 inputs the referee admits per epoch, already make every poll take longer than two Ethereum blocks.
candidates.reachability: Always reachable: the InputBox accepts any number of inputs and the referee assigns up to 2^24 of them to one epoch. Measured with the real prt-epoch.lua on a fake chain, after all inputs were delivered, for one poll of one new empty block: 0.19 s with 1,000 inputs, 31.8 s with 100,000, 158.5 s with 400,000 (extrapolating n log n, hours near the limit per epoch).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no; the trigger is the input-sending capability of section 7, and the exclusion about 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields' does not cover inputs. 2 Role: support (AUDIT.md component table); section 3: Medium 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. 3 High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'. In the honest-operator role the High case 'multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor' does not fit, because the factor grows with n. 4 Critical in the stood-for role: R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match' (here the cost per input grows with the number of blocks and inputs of the epoch), and R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and 'defends every epoch whose dispute is open, including while it processes the inputs of later epochs'. 5 Low: not reached.
candidates.threat_to_goal: While epoch N is disputed, the adversary floods epoch N+1 with inputs. Each pass of the honest player first spends the poll time of epoch N+1's listener, so each of the honest claim's bisection answers in epoch N is delayed by it; with the delay above the response budget the honest clock drains over the roughly 46 answers of a 92-level dispute and the honest claim is timed out (section 1, completeness failure: 'cannot respond in time'). A7 cannot size for it because the cost is not bounded per input.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERCHAIN/pollcost.lua N: inputs=1000 poll_of_one_empty_block=0.190s; inputs=100000 31.821s; inputs=400000 158.496s (single core, in-tree build, logs of 500 inputs per block with 300-byte payloads).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test on a fake chain that counts work instead of time: wrap eth.small (or the comparator) with a counter, deliver n inputs, advance the tip by one empty block, poll, and assert that the number of conversions/comparisons made by that poll is bounded by a constant independent of n (run for n = 1,000 and n = 10,000 and require the same count). Exit 1 on audit/prt2, where the count grows as n log n.

candidates.title: crisium keeps and rescans every consensus log since deployment to find each seal, and a restart refetches that whole range, so per-epoch and restart costs grow with the application's age
candidates.component: PRT player process (doc/recipes/crisium.lua get_seal/open_epochs with doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua)
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua lines 207-220 (seal_history = log_history.new(chain); get_seal: seal_history:observe(chain:head()); for every log of get_logs(consensus, first_block): abi:event(log) until the wanted EpochSealed), line 230 (called for every epoch opened, with first_block = getDeploymentBlockNumber()); doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua fetch (first page is the whole range, halved on failure, doubled on success).
candidates.description: To open the listener of epoch N, crisium looks up the seal of epoch N-1 by fetching all logs of the consensus contract from its deployment block to the tip, with no topic filter, into a history that is never trimmed, and by decoding them one by one from the oldest until the seal is found; the wanted seal is always among the newest, so each lookup decodes the whole history. Memory therefore grows with every past epoch, each new epoch costs work proportional to the number of past epochs, and a relaunched process, which starts with an empty history, issues eth_getLogs over the application's entire lifetime before it can open its first listener. With providers that cap the block range of a request, the pager oscillates between a failing and a succeeding page size, so the number of requests at every restart is proportional to (blocks since deployment) / (provider range limit). The lookup also reads at the chain tip rather than at the input policy, unlike every other observation of the process.
candidates.trigger: No adversary action is needed; time does it. A chain-level adversary only has to make the honest process restart (or wait for one) late in the application's life, when the restart must walk the whole range again while the dispute clocks run.
candidates.reachability: Always reachable by code reading: get_seal is called from open_epochs for every epoch whose checkpoint exists, and at every process start for the first epoch played; first_block is the consensus deployment block. Not measured against a live provider.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (no reorganization, no host fault). 2 Role: support (AUDIT.md component table); section 3: Medium 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. 3 High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'. 4 Critical in the stood-for role: R12 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records, and restarting, has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match ... That total must not grow with the application's age, with the number of past epochs, or with chain activity that does not belong to the application.' and R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim.' 5 Low: a reviewer may read the growth (a few logs per epoch) as too small to matter and rate Low; the rule text has no threshold, and the restart cost is driven by block range, not by log count.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It violates R12 as written. The practical threat is the restart path: the time a relaunched honest player needs before it resumes defending grows without bound with the age of the application, and that time is charged to the honest clock of whatever match is open (R4, A7).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. Each DaveConsensus epoch emits at least EpochStaged and EpochSealed (plus one SentryClaim per sentry); none of them is ever dropped from seal_history, and get_seal has no cache of decoded events.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test with a fake chain that records eth_getLogs ranges and counts abi:event calls: simulate E sealed epochs, start the lookup for epoch E, and assert that (a) the requested range does not start at the deployment block when a checkpoint for epoch E exists (the previous seal can be bounded by the checkpoint or read from getCurrentSealedEpoch), and (b) the number of decoded logs is independent of E. Exit 1 on audit/prt2, where both grow with E.

candidates.title: Epoch listener aborts with 'epoch log history was truncated' when a reorganization shallower than a numeric input policy leaves the canonical tip at a lower height
candidates.component: PRT epoch listener (doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua) with doc/recipes/prt-rpc.lua head() and doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua observe()
candidates.role: Support (stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua methods:poll lines 30-34 and line 52 (assert(#logs >= #self.applied, "epoch log history was truncated")); doc/recipes/prt-rpc.lua methods:head (numeric policy = tip - k); doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua observe/rewind (logs after the new head are dropped).
candidates.description: With a numeric input policy k (the demo uses 8; crisium accepts any depth), the listener observes block tip - k. If the canonical tip's number decreases (a reorganization of at most k blocks onto a branch that is momentarily shorter, which fork-choice rules that are not longest-chain allow), the observed block number decreases too. The history then drops the logs of the blocks above the new observed block although they are still canonical and already applied, and poll() fails its assertion instead of waiting. The error is uncaught, so the validator process exits and is relaunched by the supervisor; the relaunch reopens every stored epoch and replays its events. The dispute bridge handles the same situation without failing (it re-derives everything from the logs it has), so only the listener of an epoch that is still accumulating is affected. With the default policy 'finalized' the observed block cannot move backwards and the defect does not show.
candidates.trigger: A reorganization shallower than the operator's numeric policy whose new head has a lower block number than the old one, while an epoch is accumulating and the dropped blocks hold one of its logs. A chain-level adversary cannot force one without proposing blocks; it only exploits those that occur.
candidates.reachability: Reproduced with the real prt-epoch.lua on a fake chain: policy 2, input in block 8, tip 10; blocks 9 and 10 replaced by a single block 9 (block 8 unchanged). The next poll raises 'prt-epoch.lua:52: epoch log history was truncated'.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: not excluded: 'Reorganizations of the chain deeper than the operator's input policy' are out of scope, this one is shallower, and the block the policy treats as final is not replaced. 2 Role: support. 3 High/Medium cases: Medium only under the reading that the abort is 'A crash ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process' in the honest-operator role (then 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium'). 4 Critical in the stood-for role under that reading: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'. 5 Low under the other reading: the process is relaunched and R4's 'After a stop, it restarts ... and keeps defending its claim' holds, so no rule is violated and it is 'a real defect that violates no rule'. Deciding facts: whether an avoidable process exit on canonical chain data counts as a crash under section 8, and how long a relaunch takes against the clocks.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Each such reorganization costs the honest player one stop and relaunch, with the reopening of its stored epochs and the refetch of its logs charged to its dispute clock; repeated often enough during a dispute it removes margin, but one occurrence does not eliminate the honest claim.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERCHAIN/tipdown.lua: 'delivered 1' then 'false .../doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua:52: epoch log history was truncated'.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test on a fake chain: listener with input_policy = 2, one applied input in the observed block, then lower the tip by one with the observed block unchanged and poll again. Required: poll returns without error and without delivering anything twice (exit 0); on audit/prt2 it raises (exit 1).

not_covered: The Dave Tournament state machine in depth (clock arithmetic, refund and bond economics, strategies that need a bonded claim): read only for what a party without a claim can call or front-run; no defect found there at that depth.

Output validation of cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 (LibMachineValidityProof, LeafProof and the solidity-step-0.15.0 constants it imports) and whether a front-run stageTournamentResult can stage a different outputs root.

Worst-case gas of winLeafMatch against per-transaction limits: prt-transactions.lua signs min(2 x estimate, block gas limit) and knows no per-transaction gas cap (EIP-7825). Only the witness size was measured (93,992 bytes for a 65,536-byte input on the bare-metal template, below a 128 KB pool limit); gas was not measured on a chain.
No run on a live chain: reorganizations, fee manipulation, mempool replacement and the journal were analysed by reading; all experiments used fake-chain fixtures with the real Lua modules.

Racy assertions in prt-transactions.lua submit (eth_getTransactionCount and eth_call pinned with requireCanonical to a tip that is replaced between two requests fail 'transaction preflight RPC failure' and end the process): noted, not tested, not reported as a candidate.

Stale joins after a reorganization, including a root or child address reused by a different tournament because factory.instantiate is permissionless (prt-lua-bridge.md documents the stale root join; the loss is a bond, not analysed further).
Fee-ceiling and insufficient-funds behaviour under sustained congestion, and the 15% per replacement escalation of the priority fee at one nonce.
prt-websocket.lua, prt-signer.lua, prt-command.lua, prt-deploy.lua and the demo harness.
The sentinel's watch path beyond the code it shares with the validator.
Chains where block.number is not the chain's own block count (the tournament clocks use block.number).
The memory the listener and history keep per input of an open epoch (input bytes are held several times) against what a deployment is sized for.
